title: Neferine alleviated corticosterone-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice via the inhibition of TNF/NF-kappaB pathway by binding to PPARgamma.
authors: Zhao, Chen-di; Liu, Nan-Feng; Samad, Abdus; Tian, Zhen; Xu, Hong-Mei; Tian, Jiao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物Neferine通过结合PPARgamma抑制TNF/NF-kappaB通路缓解小鼠抑郁行为，核心是药物-蛋白互作，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Depression is a widespread neuropsychiatric disorder with the current therapeutic approaches achieving only suboptimal efficacy. Neferine is the main bioactive component of Nelumbinis plumula with multiple pharmacological functions. This study sought to investigate the antidepressant activity of neferine and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology analysis was performed to uncover the molecular targets and pathways involved in neferine's antidepressant effects. The interaction of neferine with the core target was demonstrated by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation. The mouse model of depression triggered by chronic corticosterone (CORT) administration was utilized to validate the impact of neferine on core targets and pathways. We found that neferine remarkably attenuated CORT-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice. A total of 178 overlapping targets were acquired through the intersection of neferine and depression-related genes. The protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis revealed nine pivotal hub genes, namely AKT1, TNF, ESR1, PPARG, JUN, HIF1A, CASP3, NFKB1, and MMP9. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these targets predominantly mapped to the TNF signaling pathway in depression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation showed that neferine has strong binding stability with PPARgamma, a key molecule involved in regulating the TNF pathway. The results of animal experiments found that a PPARgamma antagonist abolished neferine-induced alleviation of depressive-like behaviors. Moreover, neferine suppressed TNF/NF-kappaB pathway activation and attenuated neuronal loss in the hippocampus, potentially through activating PPARgamma. Collectively, our study suggested that neferine produced antidepressant effects by suppressing hippocampal inflammation and neuronal loss through inhibiting the TNF/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. These preclinical evidence laid a foundation for further exploring the role of neferine in treating depression.
abstract_zh: 抑郁症是一种广泛存在的神经精神疾病，当前的治疗方法仅能达到次优疗效。Neferine是莲子心（Nelumbinis plumula）的主要生物活性成分，具有多种药理功能。本研究旨在探讨neferine的抗抑郁活性并阐明其潜在机制。通过网络药理学分析揭示neferine抗抑郁作用涉及的分子靶点和通路。通过分子对接和分子动力学模拟证明neferine与核心靶点的相互作用。利用慢性皮质酮（CORT）给药诱导的小鼠抑郁模型验证neferine对核心靶点和通路的影响。我们发现neferine显著减轻了CORT诱导的小鼠抑郁样行为。通过neferine与抑郁相关基因的交集共获得178个重叠靶点。蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析揭示了九个关键枢纽基因，即AKT1、TNF、ESR1、PPARG、JUN、HIF1A、CASP3、NFKB1和MMP9。功能富集分析表明这些靶点主要映射到抑郁中的TNF信号通路。分子对接和分子动力学模拟显示neferine与PPARgamma（一种参与调控TNF通路的关键分子）具有强结合稳定性。动物实验结果发现PPARgamma拮抗剂消除了neferine诱导的抑郁样行为缓解作用。此外，neferine抑制了TNF/NF-kappaB通路激活并减轻了海马区神经元损失，可能通过激活PPARgamma实现。总体而言，我们的研究表明neferine通过抑制TNF/NF-kappaB信号通路来抑制海马炎症和神经元损失，从而产生抗抑郁效果。这些临床前证据为进一步探索neferine在治疗抑郁症中的作用奠定了基础。
